The Henon–Heiles describes a celestial system of a star inside of a effective potential of a galaxy. It is a well understood and results can be compared to existing results. 

### Hénon-Heiles potential

$$\Epot(x,y)=\frac{m\omega^2}{2}(x^2+y^2)+\alpha(x^2y-\frac{y^3}{3})$$


::: {layout-ncol=2}
![3D with contour lines.](/figures/henon-heiles/potential_3D-a1-m1-w1.png)

![Contour plot.](/figures/henon-heiles/potential_contour-a2-m1-w1.png)
:::

### Hamiltonian & equations of motion

$$\begin{align}
\HH(x,y,p_x,p_y) &= \Ekin(p_x, p_y) + \Epot(x,y) \\
=&\frac{(p_x^2+p_y^2)}{2m} + \frac{m\omega^2}{2}(x^2+y^2)+\alpha(x^2y-\frac{y^3}{3}) \\
\overset{\alpha=1, m=1, \omega=1}{\longrightarrow}\, &\frac{(p_x^2+p_y^2)}{2} + \frac{(x^2+y^2)}{2}+(x^2y-\frac{y^3}{3}).
\end{align}
$$

---

We obtain the equations of motion $(\dot{x_i}\equiv\tfrac{\partial x_i}{\partial t})$ by 

::: {.columns}

::: {.column}
$$
\dot{q_i} =\frac{\partial H}{\partial p_i} = \frac{\partial\Ekin}{\partial p_i}
$$ 
:::
::: {.column}
$$
\dot{p_i} =-\frac{\partial H}{\partial q_i} = -\frac{\partial \Epot}{\partial q_i} \\
$$
:::
:::

- canonical conjugate variables $(p_i,q_i)_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$ labeled by $i\in (1,2 \dots, n)$. 
- In our case simply $q_i\in\{x,y\}$ and $p_i\in\{p_x, p_y\}$ span the phase space 
- phase space: $\textbf{x}=(\textbf{p}, \textbf{q}) \in \mathbb{R}^N$, $N=4$. 

---

It may be helpful to define the following:

- $\HH(\textbf{x},t)= \HH(\textbf{p},\textbf{q},t)\equiv \HH(x,y,p_x,p_y)$,
- $\Ekin(\textbf{p})\equiv\Ekin(p_x, p_y)=\Ekin(p_x)+\Ekin(p_y)$,
- $\Epot(\textbf{q})\equiv\Epot(x,y)$ and finally
- $\Epot(y)=\Epot(0,y)$ or $\Epot(x)=\Epot(x,0)$


---

The equations of motion are then derived by $\dot{q_i} =\tfrac{\partial H}{\partial p_i}$ and $\dot{p_i} = -\frac{\partial \Epot}{\partial q_i}$ resulting in 

$$\begin{align} x&=\frac{p_x}{m} &\longrightarrow & &p_x \\
y&= \frac{{p_y}}{m} &\longrightarrow & &p_y\\
p_x&= -m\omega^2\,x - 2\alpha\, xy &\longrightarrow & & -x-2xy \\
p_y&=  -m\omega^2 y - \alpha (x^2-y^2) &\longrightarrow & &-y- x^2+y^2
\end{align}$$ 

### surface of section

To understand our 4-dimensional phase space:

1) the system is bound by Energy $E$ available
$$\HH(\textbf{x})=E=\Ekin(\textbf{p})+\Epot(\textbf{q})$$

2) Due to $\Ekin(p_i)\geq 0$
$$\Rightarrow \;E\geq\Ekin(p_y)+\Epot(\textbf{q})$$
with equality if and only if $p_x=0$

3) check for periodic orbits, create surface of section $\sufsec\in\mathbb{R}^2$ at $x=0, p_x\geq0$,
$$E\geq\Ekin(p_y)+\Epot(y)$$

4) find the boundary of the possible phase space points passing $\sufsec$, i.e. 
$$\{(y,p_y) | E=\Ekin(p_y)+\Epot(y)\}$$

---


## Implementation

The resulting equation of motion in julia code:
```julia
function equations!(du, u, p, t)
    a, m, w = p 
    x, y, px, py = u
    du[1] =  px
    du[2] =  py
    du[3] = -m*w^2*x - 2a*x*y
    du[4] = -m*w^2*y - a*(x^2 - y^2)
end
```

---


Here the potential and kinetic energy are defined:
```julia
potential(x, y, p) = p[2]*p[3]^2/2 *(x^2+y^2) + p[1]*(x^2*y - y^3/3)

kinetic(px, py, p) = (px^2 + py^2)/(2*p[2])

hamiltonian(x, y, px, py, p) = kinetic(px, py, p) + potential(x,y, p)
```

---

The equations of motion are solved by use of the package[@DifferentialEquations2017]. The data for the surface of section is gathered in runtime of the solver. This is achieved by creating a 'callbackfuntion', conditioned on $x=0, p_x\geq0$, appending $(y,p_y)$ to their respective lists:
```julia
function section_callback(section_q, section_p)
    condition(u, t, integrator) = u[1]
    affect!(integrator) = begin
        if integrator.u[3] >= 0
            push!(section_q, integrator.u[2])
            push!(section_p, integrator.u[4])
        end
    end
    ContinuousCallback(condition, affect!)
end
```
The trajectory gets solved as followed
```julia
function solve_trajectory(u0, p, tspan, dt; callback=nothing)
    prob = ODEProblem(equations!, u0, tspan, p)
    solve(prob, Vern9(), abstol=1e-10, reltol=1e-10, saveat=dt, callback=callback)
end
```


### Results

Due to $E\geq \Ekin(p_y)+\Epot(y)$ we can obtain a boundary of our plot for our surface of section, which correspond to $x=0, p_x=0$.

- solve $E-(\Ekin(p_y)+\Epot(y))=0\Rightarrow (p_y,y)$?
- $p_y=0$ to obtain 3rd-order polynomial: $E-\Epot(y)=0\Rightarrow (y_\text{min}, y_\text{max})$
- numerically determine $E-(\Ekin(p_y)+\Epot(y))=0\Rightarrow (p_y,y)$ for $y\in(y_\text{min}, y_\text{max})$
